purpose: Empirical probe of the practice sim broker's order-rejection behavior, to design reject/UNKNOWN acceptance tests. Practice account only; all probe orders cancelled; account left flat. Not strategy performance.
account: authorized ordinary U.S. practice account (SIMULATE, market 100, type 1); ID redacted; competition account never addressed

probes.result: ACCEPTED as WORKING (status 2, cum 0); not rejected; cancelled
ACCEPTED as WORKING (status 2, cum 0); not rejected; cancelled
ACCEPTED as WORKING (status 2, cum 0); not rejected; cancelled
REJECTED at API: rc 1, '[SERVER_ERROR] backend business error'; NO order_id created; no history row

findings: The sim broker is permissive: valid-format orders with invalid/non-marketable prices rest as WORKING rather than REJECTED. No status-6 (REJECTED) history row was produced for any valid-symbol probe.

Genuine broker-side rejection occurs for unknown symbols as an API error with no order created. Through PaperExecutor this surfaces as no verified acknowledgement -> order status UNKNOWN (reservation retained), the ambiguous-acknowledgement path.

A never-created UNKNOWN order has no broker_order_id and no history row, so it cannot be reconciled via read_history_order (which requires an owned broker_order_id present in history). Recovering it requires confirming absence in broker history/positions and then releasing the reservation — a dedicated UNKNOWN-recovery path.
The instrument guard ({US.AAPL, US.SPY}) intentionally restricts reconciliation; an unknown-symbol reject test would require a reviewed extension.
implication_for_gate: Broker status-6 REJECTED evidence is not obtainable for valid symbols in this permissive sim; the meaningful adverse acknowledgement path is UNKNOWN (submit error/timeout). Unit tests cover UNKNOWN fail-closed + no-blind-retry; a live reconciled UNKNOWN-recovery acceptance test requires the dedicated recovery path.
